questions.question: When does the `register()` function exported from `instrumentation.ts` run?
options: Once when a new Next.js server instance starts, before it handles requests
questions.explanation: register() is called once per server instance and must complete before the server is ready. Client-side setup belongs in instrumentation-client.ts.

questions.question: Why is the error's `digest` useful inside `onRequestError`?
options: It contains the full stack trace from the browser
It encrypts the error before sending it
It lets you correlate the server log entry with the generic error the user saw, since React may have processed the original error
It tells Next.js to retry the request
questions.explanation: Errors thrown during Server Component rendering may be transformed by React. The digest ties the server-side report to the error shown in error.tsx.

questions.question: Where does `console.log` inside a Server Component's render appear?
options: Only in the browser DevTools console
In the server's output (terminal or platform logs), not the browser
Nowhere; logging is stripped from Server Components
In both the browser and the server, always
questions.explanation: Server Components never run in the browser, so their logs go to server stdout. It is Client Components that log in both places, because they also render on the server for the initial HTML.

questions.question: Why is `useReportWebVitals` typically placed in its own small component rendered from the root layout?
options: It must run before the server starts
Web Vitals can only be measured in Server Components
It requires "use client", so isolating it keeps the client boundary small instead of turning the whole layout into a Client Component
questions.explanation: The hook needs a Client Component. A dedicated WebVitals component confines the client boundary to that component.
